name: China economy
summary: China's October consumer prices rose 0.7% and factory-gate prices 5.7%, so no deflation; credit demand stays weak
state: China's consumer prices rose 0.7% in the year to October and producer prices 5.7%, the fastest factory-gate inflation in nearly four and a half years (CGTN; New Straits Times, citing NBS data). That rules out deflation, though new bank lending was weak in October as the prolonged property downturn held back household borrowing. Searches on 14 Nov found no new developer default wave or financial contagion; October activity data are due in mid-November.
for_you: Weak credit demand in China mainly affects exporters of commodities and capital goods to China. Rising Chinese factory-gate prices can feed through to the cost of imported manufactured goods elsewhere.
rubric_hit: Normal: CPI +0.7% so no deflation; no renewed developer defaults or contagion (Watch criteria not met)

sources.title: CGTN — China's October CPI up 0.7%, PPI rises 5.7%
New Straits Times — China's factory-gate inflation at fastest in nearly 4-1/2 years in October

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
